In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
anthocyanin is an endogenous factor which antagonizes ABA and prevents stomatal opening.
the stomatal closure in epidermal tissues is not only dependent on the concentration of ABA, but also on the concentration of anthocyanin.

anthocyanins are antagonistic to stomatal opening by ABA and this is probably a mechanism by which anthocyanins prevent excessive stomatal opening and water loss in pigmented leaves or regions of the leaves.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the stomata in the epidermal strips are not responsive to ABA, whereas the stomata in intact green leaves are responsive to ABA.
stomata in anthocyanin rich leaves or leaf parts are insensitive to ABA, and the endogenous anthocynanins in these regions antagonize ABA in stomatal closure.
the stomata in anthocyanin-containing leaves are insensitive to ABA and hence, they remain open.
The main takeaway from our work is that
stomatal closure by ABA may be regulated differentially in different tissues and organs, depending upon their anthocyanin content.
stomatal closure is a complex mechanism and is not just a simple response to ABA.
anthocyanins can have an impact on plant physiology and can affect the stomata.
